title: What is known about 1RB1LE_1RC0RB_1RD1LF_1LA0LC_1LD0LA_---0RE
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1LE_1RC0RB_1RD1LF_1LA0LC_1LD0LA_---0RE.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
The tape holds two binary counters, U up and V down. When V runs out the machine either copies U into a new V or removes a few digits from the bottom of U and writes a new, longer V.
verdict: The question is open. The macro map (copy steps and eat steps) is now written in closed form (checked against the exact rebuild, not proved); with it the run from blank tape goes through 100 million macro steps, more than 10153,000,000 steps of the machine, without a halt. Lean proves the ticks and whole tick phases for arbitrary counters.

Where a halt would come from. Only from a rebuild after V reaches 0, and, in every case checked, only from an eat step whose walk runs through the counter to its top digits. In 100 million macro steps the longest walk read 750 of 29 million digits. The invariant that settled two sibling machines (busycoq PRs #57, #58) is about a regime where every rebuild reads the whole counter; here that is the event to exclude.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: The tick rules of the two counters
claims.text: For each of the headers 01101010101, 01101010111, 01101011101, 01101011111 the run uses, two theorems: with V odd, L 000 (100)^j 0 D>01101010101 01 R becomes L 100 (000)^j 0 D>01101010101 11 R in 6 * j + 146 steps; with V having i + 1 trailing zeros, L 000 (100)^j 0 D>01101010101 (11)^(i+1) 01 R becomes L 100 (000)^j 0 D>01101010101 (01)^(i+1) 11 R in 16 * i + 6 * j + 162 steps. That is U + 1 and V − 1 for every number j of carries and i + 1 of borrows and every tape L, R beyond (proved along the symbolic run of tools/py/bbtools/symtm.py).

claims.title: A whole run of ticks, for any counters
claims.text: Three statements about the tick configuration (up-counter U, gap, header, down-counter V, anything beyond), for counters given as arbitrary lists of binary digits rather than one pattern at a time. tick: if U is not all ones and V is not zero, the machine reaches the same configuration with U + 1 and V − 1. phase: for every k up to the value of V for which U + k still fits in U's digits, it reaches the configuration with U + k and V − k, the widths unchanged, without reading anything beyond the two counters. phase_to_zero: in particular, if U + V fits, V is counted down to 0 and U has gained exactly V. This is the step ‘then add the V ticks by arithmetic’ of the macro map, now a theorem; the macro simulator itself is still trusted code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 130 cells have been visited and 61 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: The macro map and its simulator
claims.text: At each moment V reaches 0 the tape is the clean configuration 0^inf F U 0 D> H (11)^n 1 0^inf (F the counter's top word), so the state is (H, n, N) with N the up-counter read as one number. py/rebuild.py writes that tape, runs the rebuild (tick runs of its sub-phases jumped by the proved tick rules, the rest cell by cell in C) to the next clean tick configuration (H', n', N', V'), and then adds the V' ticks of the phase by arithmetic: next state (H', n', N' + V'), steps by the closed formula of the tick costs. Tested: its first 397 states and step counts, up to about 10630 steps, equal those of py/counters.py (itself tested against tools/c/tmrun.c).

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>465</sup> steps (macro run)
claims.text: The macro run from blank tape goes through 293 rebuilds without a halt; at the end V has 1,536 digits and the step count is about 10<sup>465</sup>.

claims.title: The shape of the macro map: copy steps and eat steps
claims.text: At a V = 0 moment the header is 0110101 a 1 b 1 with two flags a, b. Fitted to computed rebuilds and then checked, not proved: if a = 0 the rebuild is a ‘copy’: the counter is kept and gets one more 1 on top (new counter N + 2n+1, n grows by 1), and a becomes 1. If a = 1 it is an ‘eat’: an even number s of low digits of N is removed, n grows by 3s/2 + 1 and the new counter is 2n' + (N >> s) − δ with 0 < δ < 23s+8; the flags may come out either way. The number s is given by the same kind of walk as for the sibling 1RB1LD_1RC0RB_1LA1RC_1LE0LA_1LF---_1LC---: with b = 0 an even N gives s = 2 and an odd N starts the walk in state Q; with b = 1 an odd N gives s = 2 and an even N starts it in state R; Q passes pairs 11, switches to R on 00 and stops on 01 or 10; R passes pairs ending in 0 and stops on a pair ending in 1. Checked against the exact rebuild: 100 random 40-digit counters with all four headers and three values of n (600 copies, 600 eats), and every 9-digit counter (1,530 copies, 1,344 eats; the all-ones counter is left out of the copy rule; 192 eats have a walk that reaches the top three digits, one of which halts); no exception. δ as a function of the digits read was not written down.

claims.title: The macro map in closed form
claims.text: The copy and eat steps written out completely, as a function of the macro state (a, b, n, N). Copy (a = 0): (1, b, n + 1, N + 2<sup>n+1</sup>). Eat (a = 1): (a', b', n', 2<sup>n'</sup> + (N >> s) − δ) with n' = n + 3s/2 + 1, where s, a', b' and δ come from one pass over the low digits b<sub>0</sub>, b<sub>1</sub>, ... of N. If b<sub>0</sub> = b: s = 2, δ = 27 − b<sub>1</sub> (b = 0) or 11 (b = 1). Otherwise the pass walks over the pairs (b<sub>1</sub>, b<sub>2</sub>), (b<sub>3</sub>, b<sub>4</sub>), ... in mode Q (b = 0) or R (b = 1), with k the number of pairs skipped since the last term. Q: (1,1) is skipped; (0,0) gives the term 2<sup>5k+9</sup> − 48·8<sup>k</sup> − 10 and switches to R; (0,1) stops with last term (2<sup>2k+3</sup> − 1) 2<sup>3k+6</sup> + 2<sup>3k+4</sup> + 1; (1,0) stops with (2<sup>2k+4</sup> − 1) 2<sup>3k+6</sup> + 2<sup>3k+4</sup> + 1 − e. R: (0,0) is skipped; (1,0) gives the term 2<sup>5k+4</sup> + 78·8<sup>k</sup> − 10 and stays in R; (0,1) stops with 2<sup>5k+5</sup> + 78·8<sup>k</sup> + 1 − e; (1,1) stops with 2<sup>5k+4</sup> + 78·8<sup>k</sup> + 1. Here e is the digit after the stopping pair, δ is the sum of the terms, each shifted left by 3 places per pair read after it, a' is the upper digit of the stopping pair in Q and the lower one in R, and b' = a' xor e. So the flag b is a borrow pending on the counter, and R is Q with a borrow pending. The formulas were fitted to computed rebuilds and then compared with the exact rebuild: all 252 classes of low digits with s ≤ 12 (b = 0 and 1), each with two values of n, and the first 279 macro steps of the run from blank tape (189 eats, 90 copies). No difference. They are not proved.

claims.title: 100 million macro steps of the map without a halt
claims.text: If the closed map is the rebuild for every counter (checked on the cases listed there, not proved), the run from blank tape goes through 100,000,000 macro steps (about a third of them copies) without an eat step whose walk reaches the top of the counter. At the end V has 510,093,834 digits, so the machine has run more than 10<sup>153,000,000</sup> steps (the last tick phase alone has more than 2<sup>510,093,832</sup> ticks).

claims.title: How long the walks get
claims.text: Of the 67 million eat steps of that run about half read s = 2 digits. Long walks are rare: s ≥ 64 in 11,488 eat steps, s ≥ 128 in 652, s ≥ 256 in 40, s ≥ 512 in 6; each doubling of s costs a factor of about 16. The longest walk read 750 digits when the counter had 29 million; after the first 3,000 macro steps no walk read more than 0.17% of the counter. This is a power-law tail, thinner than that of the sibling 1RB1LD_1RC0RB_1LA1RC_1LE0LA_1LF---_1LC--- (a factor of 8 to 10 per doubling there), so a walk across the whole counter looks very unlikely, but no bound on the walk is proved.

claims.title: What the rebuild map looks like in the run
claims.text: The 293 rebuilds of a 90-second macro run end in all four headers; 96 are copies and the others eat s = 2, 4, 6, ... digits (about half of them 2). So this machine behaves like its sibling 1RB1LD_1RC0RB_1LA1RC_1LE0LA_1LF---_1LC--- with an extra copy step: a counter that gains long blocks on top and loses a few digits at the bottom by a walk that would have to cross the whole counter for anything unusual (such as a halt) to happen. The same chance argument suggests it never halts; it is a heuristic.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. The two siblings 1RB1LC_0RC0RB_1LD0LA_1LE---_1LF1RA_1LA1LC and 1RB1LE_1RC0RB_1LD1RC_1LA1LE_1LF0LA_1LC--- have non-halting proofs in Coq in open pull requests of ccz181078/busycoq (#58 and #57; read on 12 November, not rebuilt here: Coq is not installed in this container). Their method, in plain terms: call a ‘wall’ the tape at a moment when V is 0. The proof gives a property of walls (enough spare room, and a marker: a 1 digit at a prescribed kind of position in the counter) and shows that every wall with the property runs to another wall with the property. It works there because the rebuild of those machines converts the whole counter in one go and loses only a bounded amount each time, so the marker can be followed from wall to wall. For this machine no such property was found (round 6): only the copy step converts the whole counter; the eat steps remove a few low digits by the walk and leave the rest, as in 1RB1LD_1RC0RB_1LA1RC_1LE0LA_1LF---_1LC---, and no quantity is known that every step keeps and that stops the walk before the top. No rebuild rule is proved in Lean for this machine. A known reduction, not rebuilt here: busycoq's Eqv_v3.v (entry TM411) proves in Coq that this machine halts if and only if 1RB1LE_1RC0RB_1RD0LF_1LA0LC_1LD0LA_---1RB halts.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. Started on a blank tape, this Turing machine has run for 10<sup>9</sup> steps without stopping. This page runs the real machine in your browser, shows the shape of its run, and lists what is known, each result marked by what it rests on.

facts.text: No halt with the closed macro map (checked, not proved); 10<sup>465</sup> steps in the exact macro simulation.
Tick rules proved in Lean for every carry and borrow.

sections.heading: Two binary counters on one tape
html: Run the machine for a while and the tape sorts itself into two numbers written in binary. On the far left, after a single 1 that acts as a sentinel, is a counter U whose digits are blocks of 3 cells: 000 is a 0 and 100 a 1, most significant digit on the left. Then come a short gap 0, the head in state D, and a fixed header such as 01101010101. Right of the header is a second counter V whose digits are pairs, least significant first: 01 is a 1 and 11 a 0.

The tick configuration is 1 U 0 D>01101010101 V. Every tick adds 1 to U and takes 1 from V. Most of the time nothing else happens.

This machine was listed as a single, but it runs the same scheme with 3-cell digits on the left (000 for 0, 100 for 1), a one-cell gap and a longer header; its ticks are slower (a constant of 146 steps) and its resets come much more often.

sections.heading: One tick: U + 1, V − 1
html: The head walks left through the trailing 1-digits of U, turning them into 0-digits (the carries), writes a 1-digit, then walks right to V and turns its trailing 0-pairs into 1-pairs and its lowest 1-pair into a 0-pair (the borrows). Written with j carries and i + 1 borrows:

beforeaftersteps
L 000 (100)^j 0 D>01101010101 01 RL 100 (000)^j 0 D>01101010101 11 R6 * j + 146
L 000 (100)^j 0 D>01101010101 (11)^(i+1) 01 RL 100 (000)^j 0 D>01101010101 (01)^(i+1) 11 R16 * i + 6 * j + 162

These two shapes are proved in Lean for every j and i (lean/Rules.lean), for every header the run has used (01101010101, 01101010111, 01101011101, 01101011111). Because the cost of a tick depends only on the numbers of carries and borrows, a long run of ticks has an exact cost: the sum of the trailing zeros of the numbers U+1, ..., U+k and V−k+1, ..., V, which has a closed form. The accelerated simulator uses it to skip billions of ticks at once.

sections.heading: The rebuild as a function of the counter
html: When V reaches 0 the tape is clean, 0^inf F U G S>H (11)^n 1 0^inf, and the machine's state is (H, n, N): header, length of V, and the up-counter read as one number together with its top word F. The rebuild then runs to the next clean tick configuration (H', n', N', V'), and the phase adds V' to the counter: the next state is (H', n', N' + V').

Here the digits are 3 cells (000 = 0, 100 = 1), the gap is a single 0 and there is no top word. The rebuild runs through tick-like sub-phases with longer headers before it reaches the next clean tick configuration.

sections.eyebrow: The macro map in one formula
sections.heading: Try a macro step on any counter
html: The copy and eat steps can be written out completely. The formulas were fitted to computed rebuilds and agree with the exact rebuild on every case tried; they are not proved. Type a counter in binary and choose the two flags of the header; the page shows what the step reads, what is subtracted, and the next state.

Copy (a = 0): N gets one more 1 on top, n grows by 1, a becomes 1. Eat (a = 1): s low digits are removed and the next counter is 2n' + (N >> s) − δ, n' = n + 3s/2 + 1. If the lowest digit equals b the step reads two digits. Otherwise it walks over pairs of digits: in mode Q it skips pairs 11, stops at a mixed pair, and at 00 changes to mode R; in mode R it skips 00, passes pairs whose upper digit is 0, and stops at the first pair whose upper digit is 1. The flag b is a borrow pending on the counter; mode R is mode Q with a borrow pending.

sections.heading: Halting, reduced to the rebuild map
html: Ticks never halt, so a halt can only come from a rebuild. There are two kinds. A copy step keeps the counter and adds a 1 on top. An eat step reads the counter from the bottom by a simple walk over pairs of digits (passing ones, then zeros, stopping at the first 1 in the right kind of position), removes what it read and puts a long new block on top. In every case computed, an eat step that stops before the top digits does not halt.

So a halt would need one walk to cross the whole, ever-growing counter. That looks very unlikely, but nobody has a rule that forbids it: two sibling machines were settled by others with a property kept from one V = 0 moment to the next, and no such property has been found here. The question is open.

family: Up/down two counters with resets (G12 family 3b)
summary: Up/down counters; ticks and whole tick phases proved in Lean; macro map (copy/eat steps with a digit walk) in closed form (checked, not proved); with it no halt in 10^8 macro steps (more than 10^153,000,000 steps); open.
